title: Degreewise invertibility of explicit principal Cech regrouping
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $r\in\mathbb N$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}r\to A$, and $F$ an integer-indexed cochain complex of module sheaves on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Write $C_p(F)$ for the product column of [def-sc-principal-cech-columns] and $T^n(F)=\prod_{J\ne\varnothing}\Gamma(D(\prod_{j\in J}f_j),F^{n+1-|J|})$ for the explicit terms of [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total]. Let $B$ be an integer-indexed bicomplex of $A$-modules and let $e_p:B^{p,\bullet}\cong C_p(F)$ be arbitrary isomorphisms of vertical complexes. Define $R^n:(\operatorname{Tot}B)^n\to T^n(F)$ by the diagonal coproduct universal property [def-sp-double-complex-total]: on the $(p,q)$ summand, where $p+q=n$, apply $e_p$ in degree $q$, project to the coordinate $J$ if $|J|=p+1$, transport along $q=n+1-|J|$, and set all other coordinates to zero. Then every $R^n$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules. No compatibility of the $e_p$ with horizontal differentials is required.

proof.text:
evaluate each categorical product of section complexes in degree q. Its
projections exhibit a product of the section modules in that degree, since evaluation
preserves products. Nonempty subsets have cardinalities between 1 and r, so only
rows 0 through r-1 are nonzero. The diagonal coproduct therefore has finite support.
For each subset J, put its coordinate in the unique summand p=card(J)-1,
q=n+1-card(J), using the inverse of e p and the degreewise product identification.
Sum these finitely many coordinate insertions. This is an inverse of the displayed
map: after a subset projection only its own row survives, and on each coproduct
summand all its product projections are recovered. Empty rows are zero objects;
for r=0 both families are empty and the same argument identifies zero modules.
The proof uses no differential or boundedness of F.
